headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from Copilot consuming untrusted repo content; data leakage and compliance risks are limited by vendor-only egress and no shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, so if system_prompts_leaks content is opened or pasted into the same editor, it can be treated as instruction-like text. The pair has no documented shared channel beyond editor buffers, and B is a source-available leak repository, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_b content is opened in the same editor buffers that agent_a reads
IF agent_a is asked to act on instructions embedded in repository text
mitigations: Keep B content out of Copilot-visible buffers
Use separate editor windows/workspaces for the two agents
Add a manual review step before accepting any Copilot-generated edits
Disable Workspace apply actions for sessions reviewing untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code and open buffers, but its network egress is vendor-only and B has no documented data-touching or egress surface. There is no shared filesystem or OAuth principal documented, so leakage between them is not evidenced beyond local editor exposure.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive file in the same editor session
IF copied text from agent_a buffers is manually pasted into agent_b-related tooling
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared editor buffers
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive tasks
Clear clipboard after copying sensitive snippets
Review Copilot suggestions before sending any text externally
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write filesystem and modify git state, while B has no documented write or network capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only plausible conflict is if B is used as a content source while A edits the same repo, which is a narrow overlap rather than a default collision.
conditions: IF agent_b output is manually copied into files that agent_a also edits
IF agent_a is used on a repository while B is simultaneously consulted for the same artifacts
mitigations: Assign one agent per mutable repository at a time
Use git branches for any Copilot-assisted edits
Review diffs before commit
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits from repo context, and if B is used as a source of leaked prompts or instructions, A's output may be treated as authoritative by the operator. The pair lacks a documented verification loop, so errors can cascade from B-derived text into A-generated code changes.
conditions: IF B-derived text is used as input to Copilot suggestions
IF the operator accepts Copilot edits without diff review
mitigations: Require human diff review before applying edits
Do not feed B outputs directly into Copilot prompts
Use a checklist to verify any generated code against source material
Limit Copilot to completion-only mode during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add automated validation tests before commit

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while B is source-available and non-runnable with no data classes touched. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy review rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a repo context
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-hosted code assistance for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot sessions
Confirm internal policy before using vendor-hosted assistance
Use redacted examples instead of real records
Document retention expectations for editor telemetry
requires-engineering: route regulated workflows to approved local tools
